extracted.intended_audience: trademark classifiers, trademark examiners, IP professionals and designers who must classify figurative elements in trademarks
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the Vienna Classification (5th ed.) to assign figurative elements of trademarks to the correct category/division/section — including rules for multi-element marks, inclusions/exclusions, auxiliary sections and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement principle for multiple figurative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a mark contains multiple figurative elements, each element is placed in its appropriate category/division/section. A composite mark may therefore be classified under multiple sections corresponding to each distinct figurative element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a bottle label showing a castle + distinctive lettering is placed in the appropriate divisions/sections of categories 7 (buildings) and 27 (inscriptions/letters). A man in uniform on horseback playing a trumpet is placed in sections 2.1.2 (armed men/uniform), 2.1.20 (men mounted on horses) and 2.1.9 (musicians). Apply auxiliary sections as associated with principal sections where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 1 — Celestial bodies, natural phenomena, geographical maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers stars, comets, sun, earth/terrestrial globes/planets, moon, constellations, armillary spheres/planetaria/atomic or molecular models, natural phenomena and geographical maps/planispheres (divisions 1.1, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 1.11, 1.13, 1.15, 1.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detailed principal sections and auxiliary sections (e.g., stars by number of points, suns with rays or with landscapes/human figures, terrestrial globes with meridians or inscriptions, crescents with human beings or animals). Notes specify exclusions (e.g., sparks and asterisks not classified under stars (1.1) but elsewhere; suns represented solely by a disk without rays go to division 26.1). Auxiliary sections (A 1.1.x, A 1.3.x, etc.) list variations (one star, stars with uneven points, sun with inscriptions, sun rays types, terrestrial globe forms, map types such as physical/political/economic). Examples/notes (e.g., stars indicating military rank included) guide placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 2 — Human beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers representations of men, women, children, mixed groups/scenes, and parts of the human body including skeletons and skulls (divisions 2.1, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections list types (e.g., 2.1 men: armed men, musicians, men in costumes, men mounted on horses; 2.3 women: nuns, women in sports or professional roles; 2.5 children: babies, children playing; 2.7 mixed groups/scenes: couples, family scenes, battle scenes, indoor/outdoor tables; 2.9 body parts: hearts, eyes, ears, hands, skeletons). Notes explain placement rules (e.g., inscriptions representing a human being go to 27.3.1; heads are placed in divisions 2.1/2.3/2.5/2.7, not 2.9.25). Auxiliary sections give variants (shadows, silhouettes, seated/standing, stylized, several persons) and codify exclusions (adolescents classified elsewhere, groups that convey a scene go to 2.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 — Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifies animals and animal parts across multiple series/divisions: quadrupeds (series I–V), parts/skeletons, birds/bats, aquatic animals/scorpions, reptiles/amphibia/snails/seals, insects/spiders/micro-organisms, other animals and groups (divisions 3.1–3.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections enumerate species/groups (e.g., lions, tigers, horses, elephants, dogs, rodents, monkeys, birds by type, fish and marine creatures, insects like butterflies and bees). Auxiliary sections cover heraldic forms, stylized animals, animals in costume, poses (standing, lying, rearing), heads, parts (paws, skeletons, hides). Notes clarify exclusions (heads of quadrupeds placed in 3.1–3.5 not in 3.6.25; written/typographical animal representations go to 27.3.3). Also includes group categories and vivariums/aquariums placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 4 — Supernatural, fabulous, fantastic or unidentifiable beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes winged or horned personages, beings partly human/partly animal, fabulous animals (dragons, griffons, unicorns), personified plants/objects/geometrical figures/robots/masks and groups of figurative elements classified across divisions of category 4 (divisions 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, 4.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections list specific types (winged human heads, cherubs, centaurs, sphinx, tritons, dragons, phoenixes). Auxiliary sections and notes indicate subtypes (e.g., centaurs with weapons), exclusions (not human beings or certain dwarfs classified elsewhere), and examples (snowmen, scarecrows, ghosts classified among personified or unidentifiable heads/figures). Use auxiliary/group sections for composite or cross-divisional groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5 — Plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers trees and bushes, leaves/needles/branches, flowers/blossoms, grain/seeds/fruits, vegetables, other plants, and plant-based decorations (divisions 5.1, 5.3, 5.5, 5.7, 5.9, 5.11, 5.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections enumerate specific plants and plant elements (e.g., conifers, palms, oak leaves, roses, lilies, grapes, apples, carrots, potatoes, algae, mushrooms). Auxiliary sections specify counts/arrangements (one, two, three, more than three; stylized forms), and exclusions (surfaces/backgrounds covered with repeated plant elements are placed in 25.7.25; vine shoots vs. vine decorations distinguished between 5.3.19 and 5.13.6). Notes indicate example inclusions like heraldic flowers and coffee beans as seeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 6 — Landscapes
rubrics_metrics.description: Encompasses mountains/rocks/grottoes, landscapes with water/river/stream, desert or tropical-type landscapes, urban landscapes or village scenes, and other landscapes (divisions 6.1, 6.3, 6.6, 6.7, 6.19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections and subsequent pages define the landscape subtypes and provide the auxiliary subdivisions for particular landscape features (the chunk begins listing 6.1 Mountains, rocks, grottoes). Use the division/subdivision structure to choose the most specific match for the depicted landscape element.
